headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screenshots while RD-Agent sends data to external APIs and handles secrets, creating a plausible cross-agent exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while RD-Agent can ingest files/logs and browser/API outputs. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text from one agent steer the other, though no direct shared channel is documented here.
conditions: IF the operator copies RD-Agent output into ChatGPT Desktop or vice versa
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder or log directory
mitigations: Disable clipboard bridging during paired runs
Keep each agent on separate folders/workspaces
Review any copied text before pasting between agents
Use a human-in-the-loop step before acting on generated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, logs, and multiple API keys. RD-Agent's broad API egress plus shared user data creates a realistic exfiltration path if sensitive content is exposed to both agents.
conditions: IF sensitive files or screenshots are available to ChatGPT Desktop
IF RD-Agent is allowed to process the same sensitive workspace or logs
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared logs before running RD-Agent
Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to files and app context but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation; RD-Agent can use APIs and write logs. Direct write-write conflict is limited, but both can still contend over shared mutable resources if the operator points them at the same project artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to edit the same repository or log directory
IF RD-Agent writes outputs that ChatGPT Desktop then reads as authoritative
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only reviewer
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Use separate output directories
Add a manual merge step before committing changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can consume files, screenshots, and app context, and RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs. If one agent's output is treated as authoritative by the other, errors can cascade into incorrect analysis or actions; the profiles do not show built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are pasted into ChatGPT Desktop without verification
IF ChatGPT Desktop's summaries are used as inputs to RD-Agent workflows
mitigations: Require source-link verification before reuse
Ask the second agent to independently re-check claims
Keep a human review gate between outputs and actions
Tag unverified outputs clearly in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and external APIs. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if regulated data is routed through both systems, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PII, financial records, or secrets is processed by both agents
IF the operator relies on different retention policies across the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent logs
Confirm retention settings for both systems
Delete transient artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
